name: Tandoori Chicken
cuisine: Punjabi / North Indian (Peshawar–Delhi tandoor tradition, adapted here for a home oven/OTG, air fryer or tawa; no tandoor needed)

ingredients.name: Chicken leg, skinless, bone-in (thigh + drumstick)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 whole leg, cut at the joint into 2 pieces

ingredients.name: Lemon juice (nimbu ras)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (about ½ small lemon), for the first rub

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli powder (lal mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1¼ tsp in total (½ tsp for the first rub, ¾ tsp for the marinade)

ingredients.name: Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp in total (a pinch less than ¼ tsp for the first rub, the rest in the marinade)

ingredients.name: Hung curd (strained dahi) or thick Greek-style yoghurt
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tbsp (made from about 80 g / ⅓ cup ordinary curd strained for 30 min)

ingredients.name: Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp, crushed between the palms

ingredients.name: Mustard oil (sarson ka tel), or any cooking oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 tsp in the marinade, 1 tsp for basting)

equipment: Mixing bowl (with a lid or cling film) for marinating
Sharp knife and chopping board, for slashing the chicken
Muslin cloth or a clean thin cotton cloth plus a strainer, for hanging the curd
Oven/OTG (main method) with a wire rack and a tray lined with foil underneath
No oven, air fryer instead: 200 °C, preheat 3 min, cook 18–22 min, turning once and basting at 10 min; finish 2 min at the highest setting to char

No oven or air fryer, tawa/heavy pan instead: heat 1 tsp oil in a heavy tawa or kadai, add the pieces, cook 3 min per side on medium-high to colour, then cover with a lid and cook 12–15 min on low-medium, turning every 4 min and spooning any leftover marinade on top; uncover for the last 2–3 min to dry the coating
Tongs or two forks, for turning
Basting brush (or the back of a spoon)
Optional, for smoky flavour: one small piece of charcoal, a small steel bowl, and a lid that fits your mixing bowl or pan (step 23)

steps.title: Hang the curd (skip if using thick Greek-style yoghurt)
steps.text: Put 80 g (⅓ cup) curd in a muslin-lined strainer over a bowl and leave it in the fridge.
steps.tip: Thin, runny curd slides off the chicken and steams instead of roasting. This is the single biggest difference to the result.
steps.visualCue: Whey drips into the bowl; the curd turns thick like soft cream cheese, about 40 g left
steps.cameraCheck: The thick curd in the cloth
steps.videoShot: A spoon pulling a thick dollop of curd off the muslin.

steps.title: Pat the chicken dry
steps.text: Pat the 250 g chicken leg dry with paper towel. If it is a whole leg, cut it at the joint into thigh and drumstick.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, board and knife with soap after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Matte, not wet, surface
steps.videoShot: A paper towel pressing on the chicken.

steps.title: Slash the chicken
steps.text: Make 3 deep cuts (down to the bone) across the thigh and 2–3 across the drumstick.
steps.tip: Deep slashes let the marinade reach the bone and help the thick part cook through at the same time as the thin part.
steps.visualCue: Deep, open gashes about 1 cm apart
steps.videoShot: The knife drawing a deep cut across the thigh.

steps.title: First rub
steps.text: Sprinkle ½ tsp (1 g) Kashmiri chilli powder, a pinch of salt (about 1 g) and 2 tsp (10 ml) lemon juice over the chicken. Rub it into the slashes.
steps.visualCue: An even, red, wet coat, with colour inside every cut
steps.cameraCheck: The rubbed chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Fingers pushing red rub into a slash.

steps.title: Rest the first rub
steps.text: Cover and leave in the fridge.
steps.visualCue: The surface looks slightly paler and firmer where the lemon has touched it
steps.cameraCheck: The covered bowl going into the fridge
steps.videoShot: The bowl sliding onto a fridge shelf.

steps.title: Grate the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Grate 5 g ginger (1 tsp) and 5 g garlic (1 tsp) into a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Two small wet heaps of pale paste
steps.videoShot: Garlic being rubbed on the grater.

steps.title: Start the marinade
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, put the 40 g hung curd and the ginger-garlic. Whisk with a spoon.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, thick, flecked white paste with no lumps
steps.videoShot: A spoon whisking the curd smooth.

steps.title: Add the powders and salt
steps.text: Add ¾ tsp (1.5 g) Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp (1 g) coriander powder, ¼ tsp (0.5 g) cumin powder, ¼ tsp (0.5 g) garam masala, a small pinch of turmeric and the remaining salt (about 1.5 g, a little over ¼ tsp). Mix.
steps.visualCue: An even, deep orange-red paste, no streaks of white
steps.videoShot: Powders falling onto the white curd and being stirred in.

steps.title: Add kasuri methi and oil
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms into the bowl and add 1 tsp (5 ml) mustard oil. Mix well.
steps.tip: Using raw mustard oil? Some cooks heat it until it just smokes and cool it first to soften its sharpness; it is optional.
steps.visualCue: A glossy paste with green flecks; it should coat the spoon thickly and not run
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the bowl.

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken (with any juices) to the marinade and massage it in, pushing it into every slash.
steps.visualCue: Thick, even red coat, no bare patches
steps.videoShot: Hands turning the chicken in the red marinade.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate.
steps.tip: Longer (6 h to overnight) gives a deeper flavour, but 2 h is enough for a good result.
steps.visualCue: None needed; set a timer
steps.cameraCheck: The covered bowl in the fridge
steps.videoShot: Cling film being pressed over the bowl.

steps.title: Take the chicken out
steps.text: Take the bowl out of the fridge.
steps.tip: Cold-from-the-fridge chicken cooks unevenly; the outside chars before the bone is done.
steps.visualCue: The bowl is no longer icy cold to touch
steps.videoShot: The bowl being set down on the counter.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Set the oven/OTG to 240 °C (or its highest setting up to 250 °C), top and bottom heat, and let it heat fully.
steps.tip: Air fryer instead? Preheat it to 200 °C for 3 min and follow the times in section 3.
steps.visualCue: The oven's indicator light goes off / the beep sounds
steps.videoShot: Turning the dial and the light coming on.

steps.title: Set up the tray
steps.text: Line the tray with foil and put the wire rack on top.
steps.visualCue: A rack sitting above a foil-lined tray
steps.videoShot: Foil being pressed into the tray.

steps.title: Arrange the chicken
steps.text: Place the pieces on the rack with space between them, slashed side up. Leave the extra marinade in the bowl.
steps.visualCue: Pieces not touching
steps.videoShot: Tongs placing the pieces.

steps.title: First roast
steps.text: Put the tray on the middle shelf and roast.
steps.visualCue: The marinade has set and the edges are starting to brown
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken through the oven door
steps.videoShot: The tray sliding into the glowing oven.

steps.title: Baste and turn
steps.text: Take the tray out, brush the chicken with 1 tsp (5 ml) mustard oil (plus any leftover marinade), and turn the pieces over.
steps.tip: Work quickly so the oven does not lose its heat; close the door while you baste.
steps.visualCue: Glossy pieces, the underside now on top
steps.videoShot: The brush gliding over the chicken.

steps.title: Second roast
steps.text: Return the tray and roast.
steps.visualCue: Deep red-brown coat with dark, charred edges
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken through the oven door
steps.videoShot: Edges sizzling and darkening.

steps.title: Check it is cooked
steps.text: Insert a thermometer into the thickest part near the bone, or cut into it.
steps.tip: Still pink? Roast 4–5 min more and check again.
steps.visualCue: 74 °C (165 °F) or above; the meat is white at the bone and the juices run clear, with no pink
steps.cameraCheck: The cut-open thickest piece, or the thermometer reading
steps.videoShot: A knife opening the thigh at the bone.

steps.title: Char the outside
steps.text: Switch the oven to top heat/grill for 2–3 min, or hold each piece with tongs over a medium gas flame for 30–60 sec, turning.
steps.tip: Charring is what makes it taste "tandoori" rather than baked.
steps.visualCue: Small black charred spots on the edges of the slashes, without the whole surface burning
steps.videoShot: A piece turning over the blue gas flame, edges blistering.

steps.title: Move to a plate
steps.text: Transfer the pieces to a serving plate.
steps.visualCue: Juices on the foil stay behind
steps.videoShot: Tongs lifting the chicken off the rack.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Leave the chicken to rest, loosely covered.
steps.visualCue: Steam stops pouring off; juices settle back into the meat
steps.videoShot: A plate loosely covered with foil.

steps.title: Optional: smoke it (dhungar)
steps.text: Heat a small piece of charcoal over a gas flame until it glows (3–4 min). Put it in a small steel bowl, place the bowl in the middle of the chicken plate (or pan), pour ½ tsp ghee on the coal, and cover with a lid for 2 min.
steps.tip: Use tongs, keep the coal away from plastic, and open a window. Not counted in nutrition (a little ghee smoke, most of it burns).
steps.visualCue: Thick white smoke when the ghee hits the coal; a strong smoky smell when you lift the lid
steps.cameraCheck: The glowing coal in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Ghee hitting the coal and the lid going on.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Squeeze the lemon wedge over the chicken and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.
steps.visualCue: Red, charred pieces with bright onion and green chutney beside them
steps.videoShot: Lemon being squeezed over the chicken.

reasons: about 40 g of protein for about 365 kcal, almost no carbohydrate, no deep-frying, only 2 tsp of oil (mostly mono- and polyunsaturated mustard oil), and no sugar; the curd and spices add flavour without much energy. Points come off for sodium (about 1,150 mg, more than half the daily limit), dietary cholesterol from dark meat, very little fibre or vegetables on its own, and the small amounts of char formed at high heat. Restaurant versions are usually basted with butter, salted more heavily, often coloured with artificial red dye, and a half portion is 1.5–2× this serving.

researchRating.basis: one of the best-known Indian dishes worldwide, with a famous origin story (Moti Mahal, Peshawar and then Daryaganj, Delhi, after 1947) and the base of butter chicken; Swasthi's Recipes' restaurant-style version shows 4.99/5 from 619 votes, The Daring Gourmet 4.99/5 from 108 votes, Once Upon a Chef 4.93 from 206 reviews, and Whisk Affair 4.84/5 (12 votes); every major Indian chef site (Sanjeev Kapoor, Ranveer Brar) publishes it, and Mumbai food guides (Curly Tales, Republic World, Tripadvisor) list dozens of places known for it. Small deduction because home oven versions are often called dry or "not like the tandoor" without a char or smoking step.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 3 days; cool it within 1 hour of cooking. Freezer: up to 2 months, well wrapped. Raw marinated chicken can wait in the fridge up to about 24 h before cooking. Reheat in an oven or air fryer at 180 °C for 6–8 min (8–10 min from thawed frozen) until piping hot to the bone, or in a covered pan with 1 tbsp water for 5–6 min, turning once; the microwave works but makes the coating soft.
leftoverRemix: tandoori chicken chaat (an established dish; Sanjeev Kapoor publishes a Tandoori Murg Chaat). Pull the leftover meat off the bone and shred it. Toss with chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, a pinch of chaat masala, lemon juice, chopped coriander and 1 tbsp green chutney, and top with a few pomegranate seeds or roasted peanuts. A cold, tangy, high-protein salad or a filling for a roti wrap.
burnOff: about 5.2 km of running (365 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 7.3 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 30 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). A restaurant half (about 550–750 kcal, est.) is about 8–11 km of running.

navratri.reason: contains chicken, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains chicken and garlic, avoided under the common Ekadashi rule set (same as Navratri in the sources used).

jain.reason: contains chicken plus garlic and ginger (root).

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken; a good high-protein, low-carb iftar dish, but at about 1,150 mg sodium (est.) it is salty for sehri unless you cut the salt by half.

jain.reason: contains chicken, plus garlic and ginger (root).

sattvik.reason: contains chicken and garlic (onion is only a serving side).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or besan in the marinade, and no hing (asafoetida) used; if you sprinkle chaat masala or use a packaged tandoori masala, check the label, as many contain hing compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: the marinade is hung curd (yoghurt); use coconut yoghurt or the lemon-and-oil marinade in the Dairy-free variant (section 4).

description: A non-veg (chicken), gluten-free Punjabi grill with no flour or deep-frying; dairy-free, vegetarian (tandoori soya chaap) and low-oil versions below.

variants.reason: Jain diet excludes meat, so there is no Jain tandoori chicken. The Jain route is a paneer version without garlic and ginger: Sanjeev Kapoor publishes an established Jain Hariyali Paneer Tikka (green marinade, no onion or garlic; it uses dry ginger powder, which stricter Jain practice also skips). Paneer tikka is FitPlate dish 53 and gets its own Jain variant there.
the dish is defined by chicken. The plant-based route is the Vegetarian variant below made with soy or coconut yoghurt (Rachna Cooks lists soy yoghurt as an option for tandoori soya chaap).
main recipe already gluten-free (no flour, no hing). Check the labels of chaat masala or packaged tandoori masala if you add them.
